issues.description: Validation loop never terminates training loop; max_step check only happens between epochs, causing overshoot or infinite spin
issues.detail: run() loops while global_step < max_step, but train() runs save_interval steps unconditionally and then validates and checkpoints. There is no inner check that breaks when global_step reaches max_step. The loop invariant 'global_step in [0, max_step]' is violated; the final iteration overshoots by up to save_interval-1 steps before exiting. State the invariant and enforce it inside train().

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery sorts by int(name.split('step_')[-1]) but step_N may not be the suffix
issues.detail: The filter accepts any directory containing 'step_' anywhere in the name, then splits on 'step_' and takes the last segment as int(). If a directory is named e.g. 'step_100_backup' or contains additional underscores, int() raises ValueError. Tighten the predicate to startswith('step_') and parse name[len('step_'):], or use a regex. State the invariant on checkpoint naming.

issues.description: Validation aggregates as Python list of floats then sum/len; should reduce online
issues.detail: all_stats[key].append(value) accumulates O(N) memory per validation pass, then sum/len pays another O(N). For large validation sets this is wasteful and risks numerical drift. Maintain a running (count, sum) pair per key — O(1) memory, single pass, identical mean. Asymptotically OK, practically slow and unnecessarily allocating.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats iterates dict while reassigning stats[key]; relies on insertion-order stability and divides a SUM-reduced tensor by world_size with no count
issues.detail: The 'mean' computed by SUM/world_size is correct only if every rank contributes exactly one value per key per call. If a rank skips a stat (e.g. a key absent on some rank) the result is wrong silently — there is no key-set consistency check across ranks. At minimum assert key alignment, or all_reduce a presence mask. State this precondition in the docstring.

issues.description: trainer_args uses inconsistent keys: docstring says max_steps/val_interval, code reads max_step and never reads val_interval
issues.detail: The constructor docstring advertises max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval; the code actually reads max_step and save_interval and ignores val_interval entirely (validation runs once per save_interval). log_interval is stored but never consulted. This is a literate-programming failure: the explanation does not match the code. Reconcile names and document the actual cadence.

issues.description: Specifier parsing uses split() on whitespace; format documented as colon-delimited with optional factor — no validation, no invariant stated
issues.detail: train.py splits valid_*_specifier on whitespace and passes each token to DataIteratorFactory; no check that the token matches the documented 'task:name[:factor]' grammar. A typo silently produces a misnamed validation set keyed by the raw spec string. A small parse function with a stated grammar would catch this at startup rather than at first batch.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with two correctness bugs worth blocking on. The outer training loop has no stated invariant and overshoots max_step by up to save_interval-1 steps; checkpoint resume parses directory names with a fragile split that will crash on any near-miss naming. Validation aggregation allocates O(N) per key for a quantity computable in O(1), and the all_reduce 'mean' silently assumes key-set consistency across ranks without asserting it. Documentation drifts from code (max_steps vs max_step, unused val_interval/log_interval) — a literate-programming failure on a file whose docstring is otherwise careful. The algorithms are conventional and correct in spirit; the rigor and the reader-facing explanation are missing.
